end.parentNote: Saanvi practised building square-dot patterns by adding the next odd-number layer and found that 1+3+5+7+9 = 25 = 5². They also calculated the added dots between 5×5 and 6×6 squares as 11. Saanvi still needs to explain why three examples do not prove a rule for every case and mixed up the parity of sums of odd numbers; these points were not corrected by the end. At home, draw successive dot squares and ask Saanvi to describe the new L-shaped layer and write the general reason.
